column11: none of it, and the stage line is why. Section 1.1 of the Trodelvy label (DailyMed set id 57a597d2-03f0-472e-b148-016d7169169d, spl version 20, effective 2026-06-29, the row the book's labels table carries) covers only 'unresectable locally advanced or metastatic triple negative breast cancer (TNBC)', in first line and in second line or later, plus metastatic HR-positive HER2-negative breast cancer. ASCENT-05 (NCT05633654) is the adjuvant setting and excludes the label outright: 'Stage IV (metastatic) breast cancer as well as history of any prior (ipsi- or contralateral) invasive breast cancer' and 'Evidence of recurrent disease following preoperative therapy and surgery' are exclusion criteria, and the inclusion is 'residual invasive triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) in the breast or lymph nodes after neoadjuvant therapy and surgery'. A patient has metastatic disease or she does not, so in any one year the two pools are disjoint

(4) 0.94 without a germline BRCA mutation, which ASCENT-05 excludes ('Individuals with germline breast cancer gene (BRCA) mutations'): Lynce F, Ru M, Luo L, Miranda M, Xu X, Isaacs C, 'Real-world clinical outcomes of patients with early-stage TNBC and BRCAm who were treated with adjuvant capecitabine in the United States', Breast Cancer Res Treat 2026;218(3):41, doi 10.1007/s10549-026-08011-6, PMID 42584742, PMC13468742, US Flatiron Health records 2016 to 2024: 'Of 882 patients who received adjuvant capecitabine, 53 (6%) had BRCAm, and 829 (94%) had non-BRCAm tumors'. 0.91 x 0.294 x 0.623 x 0.94 = 0.156677, about 5,436 patients a year
column12: the weak link is filter (2) and it cuts both ways. Its denominator is stage II and III TNBC while it is applied here to all non-metastatic diagnoses including stage I, who are rarely given neoadjuvant chemotherapy, so the figure reads high. Its window is 2010 to 2013, before KEYNOTE-522 made neoadjuvant pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy the standard for stage II and III disease, and the paper itself records use rising over its own four years, 'from 2010 to 2013 (27.8% - 31.2%)', so it reads low. No current US share of stage II-III TNBC given neoadjuvant therapy was found free, which is why the dated one is carried rather than guessed at. Filter (3) is measured mostly before pembrolizumab as well, and a residual share of 62.3% is high against the 35.2% KEYNOTE-522 implies and the 37.1% the Neo-Real cohort reports, so this too reads high. Filter (4) is measured among patients who received capecitabine, and a known BRCA carrier now goes to olaparib instead, so 6% understates the carrier share of the whole residual-disease pool and this filter also reads high

Andrade MO, Bonadio RC, Ipina A, Testa L, Tavares MC, Balint FC et al., 'Treatment patterns and safety of adjuvant therapy after chemoimmunotherapy for early-stage triple-negative breast cancer: real-world data from the Neo-Real/GBECAM 0123 study', Breast Cancer Res Treat 2026;216(3):27, doi 10.1007/s10549-026-07938-0, PMID 41848921: 'Among patients with residual disease and no germline BRCA1/2 mutations (n = 207), 57.5% received pembrolizumab plus capecitabine, 26.1% pembrolizumab alone, and 12.6% capecitabine alone'. 57.5 + 12.6 = 70.1% are on a capecitabine-containing regimen. ASCENT-05 randomises against exactly that, 'Pembrolizumab or Pembrolizumab + Capecitabine', so 70.1% is the incumbent regimen the drug has to take. MULTIPLE 0.5, A JUDGEMENT: 0.5 x 0.701 = 0.3505, about 1,905 US patients a year at peak
column12: the row to argue with, and its first weakness is the anchor's geography: Neo-Real is a Brazilian and Argentine cohort and this is a US pool. The US cross-check is that capecitabine is the incumbent in the same place, 'Most patients received capecitabine after neoadjuvant treatment (BRCAm: n = 49/53, 92%; non-BRCAm: n = 755/829, 91%)' in the Flatiron series cited on the eligible_pct row, but that paper gives no denominator so it cannot set the share itself. The case for higher than 0.5: the comparator is oral capecitabine on a CREATE-X-era evidence base, the prescriber is the breast oncologist Gilead already calls on, and an invasive disease-free survival win in a curative setting moves practice fast. The case for lower: sacituzumab govitecan is an intravenous ADC with boxed neutropenia and diarrhoea warnings being offered to patients who may already be cured, Dato-DXd and other ADCs are moving into the same setting, and adjuvant therapy is a fixed course, so a share of each year's starts is the right basis but the engine's stopping rate was measured on metastatic patients
